message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data on the current air quality in Los Angeles. For the most up‑to‑date information you can check one of the following:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the latest AQI (Air Quality Index) and pollutant breakdown. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles”, and see the live AQI, forecast, and health recommendations. |
| **Local news sites** | Many local news outlets (e.g., LA Times, CBS Los Angeles) publish daily air‑quality updates. |
| **Mobile apps** | Apps like “AirVisual”, “Plume Labs: Air Report”, or the EPA’s own “AirNow” app provide real‑time readings and alerts. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, the AirNow website typically shows the current AQI, the main pollutant (e.g., PM₂.₅, ozone), and a health advisory (Good, Moderate, Unhealthy, etc.). Feel free to let me know if you’d like a summary of what those AQI categories mean!
